system.description: You twist your ankle and have 1/2 movement speed and cannot charge for 1d4+1 rounds. You have to moan as you move.
You hit an Ally with a basic attack. They need to do a DC 15 DEX save to see if they can duck out of the way or take the damage.
You fall Prone in a wildly dramatic way, muttering "Oh my, I have a case of the vapors" as you fall.
You hit yourself in the head causing a minor flesh wound with 4HP damage. You are blinded by blood flowing into your eyes for [[1d4]] rounds.
You throw your weapon/implement [[1d4]] squares in a direction based on a [[1d8]] roll (where 1 is north). If you hit a party member, they take [[1d6]] damage.
That fumble was just too much for you. As a bonus action you pull out a mug of ale and take several big pulls. You are intoxicated for [[1d4]] rounds.
The target hits you with a basic attack.

"Head's-up!" you yell our as your crappy hit misses its mark and hits one of your party members within mele range of the target. GM chooses the party member with a dice roll. Roll damage on the party member and apply half the damage to them, rounding down.
The target critically hits you with a basic attack. Double the normal damage. Ouch.
A forceful pop in your shoulder is heard as your arm goes limp. The arm you used to make the attack is incapacitated for 1d4 + 6 rounds.
An item you carry with a buff or magical effect on it flickers out like a dying candle. You can not use the item until after your next long rest.
Your Weapon/Implement is broken. You mark it as so and swap it out or use it with -5 and disadvantage. You will have to figure out if it can be repaired.
You recieve a -2 penalty to attack rolls against target until you successfully hit target with an attack.
You are dazed until end of your next turn.

You feeling lucky? How lucky? Take [[1d10]] damage or roll 1d20 and hope for the best. If you get 1-10, you roll damage on yourself. If you get 11-20, your fumble becomes a hit and you roll damage on your target. Choose wisely.
You embarrased your god. In turn, they turned the 5 foot square on which you stand to lava for this turn. You take [[1d10]] fire damage.
You critically hit an ally with a basic attack. Apply half the damage to them and half the damage to yourself. When you round, they get the brunt of it.

You let the team down. Make ammends by giving them an item from your inventory. They must accept it. You can't attack again until you complete this task. You may have something they've always wanted... or perhaps they like shiny objects.
This is a fumble, right? Well, your god feels so bad for you that they roll back time and allow you to re-roll. You lucky duck!
You're not sure what happened, but your spell blew up in your face. You take the damage + 6. If you did not cast a spell, just take [[1d10]] damage.
Your knee hyperextends awkwardly. You have 1/4 movement speed and cannot charge for [[1d4+6]] rounds.
Every party member donates 2 HP to your target. You donate 4 HP.
Lightening strikes you, as if punishing you for such a crappy roll. Take 1d6 lightening damage.

You feel the love, and bee-line to the closest party member for a mega-hug. They are grappled until they break your grapple. You can not choose to let go... it is love afterall. If your target was within mele and you moved away, they do get an opportunity attack.
You really anger your target. How dare you make such a feeble attempt against their clear badassery. They roll with advantage for the next [[1d4]] rounds.
Your weapon is jacked. You must spend your next action fixing it with found objects around you.
You are stunned until the end of your next turn.
You are weakened until end of your next turn.
Your attack confuses your party and any rangers attack you, by accident, with disadvantage. If you are a ranger, you attack yourself, foolishly, with advantage.
The power of dance compells you! You dance uncontrollably until the end of the next round and suffer 1 level of exhaustion.
You can not speak until the end of combat. Your party members are likely delighted by this.
Your spell feeds back to you, doing its damage and effects on yourself. If you didn't cast a spell, you got lucky.

Your opponent parries your awkward attack that causes you to hit yourself in the groin. You have 1/2 movement and -4 to all actions for [[1d6+4]] rounds. Your eyes water, so you are blind until the end of your next turn.

It has been a while since you've bathed... and that last attack really worked up a sweat. You stink. Your party members must only refer to you as "Stinky Pete" until your next long rest, which must include bathing.
You hit yourself with same attack you fumbled with, receiving all negative conditions and effects of the attack. Dummy.
You reach for your flask to calm your nerves, but you accidentally grab poison. You are poisoned for [[1d10]] rounds or until someone addresses the medical issue.
Take [[1d8]] damage or deal [[1d10]] damage to one of the other party members. Your choice. Have fun with it.
Wow, I mean, what were you thinking? This didn't work out quite like you'd planned, and your target rolls damage on you instead.

In an embarrasing move, you cut loose part of your armor and receive a -5 penalty until armor is fixed. Fixing the armor will require [[1d3]] rounds of performing no other action. Good luck with that.

A copy of you appears next to you. They are filled with self-hate, embarrased by your fumble. They steal 5 HP from you, and take their turn right before you in each round until dead. Consider therapy.
